summary: Build practical emergency preparedness, triage, drills, and continuity skills. Develop response artefacts you can apply across facilities. Enquire today.
lede: Workplace emergency preparedness helps facility, safety, security and business continuity professionals coordinate responses to disruptive events. It covers assessing facility hazards and impacts, prioritizing incidents, assigning response roles and escalation paths, and activating continuity measures to protect critical services. Participants also practice designing drills, reviewing performance and documenting corrective actions through work such as risk registers, incident plans and after-action reports.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who coordinate people, facilities, safety information, and operational decisions during disruptive events. It suits both developing practitioners and experienced role holders who need a structured way to test and improve site response capability.
prerequisites: You should have at least six months of exposure to facility operations, HSE, security, business continuity, emergency coordination, or incident management. No programming is required, and you do not need prior certification in ISO 22301:2019, ISO 22320:2018, or the Incident Command System. Bring a current site procedure, anonymized drill record, or example incident checklist if available. Advanced digital topics remain at operational application level, using supplied datasets and templates rather than technical engineering or software development.
